title: Genetic investigation in idiopathic intracranial hypertension
summary:
Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) is a rare condition characterized by increased intracranial pressure without an identifiable cause. The etiology of the disease remains unclear. The most common symptoms of IIH are headaches and visual disturbances.  
Retrospective studies report a familial occurence in about 10% of IIH cases. To date, no genetic testing has been performed in cases of IIH with familial clustering or atypical phenotype.  
The specialized clinic at Charité - Universitätsmedizin Berlin cares for IIH patients from all over Germany.  
Through whole genome sequencing (next generation sequencing), a comprehensive genetic investigation of IIH patients with indications of a genetic predisposition will be conducted.  
In addition to understanding the pathogenesis, the identification of genetic forms could facilitate the development of causal therapies and allow more precise prognostic assessments.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Confirmed IIH diagnosis according to the revised Friedman criteria & indications of a genetic predisposition (normal weight patients, male individuals, familial clustering, fulminant course).
Exclusion criteria:
IIH without papilledema (IIHWOP), possible IIH, secondary intracranial hypertension
